title: Landon Emenalo renews Chelsea contract through to 2031
content:
Chelsea youth-team player Landon Emenalo has signed a new long-term contract that commits him to Stamford Bridge until June 2031.

The 18-year-old, son of former Chelsea technical director Michael Emenalo, is one of the club’s most highly-regarded academy prospects, having initially joined in the under-8 age group.

A versatile player capable of playing at left-back, centre-back and in central midfield, Emenalo has participated in first-team training sessions under each of Mauricio Pochettino, Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior. The teenager has also featured in matchday squads in the Premier League, Champions League and Conference League.

Having signed his first professional contract with Chelsea shortly after his 17th birthday in January 2025, Emenalo has now committed his long-term future to the club with a deal covering the next five years.

Emenalo briefly left Chelsea’s academy when his father resigned as technical director in 2017 and became Monaco sporting director, with Landon joining the French club’s youth ranks, but he returned to Cobham as an under-13 soon after the family moved back to England two years later.

He has represented both England and the United States at youth level — having been born in Tuscon, Arizona to a U.S. mother — and is also eligible to play for Nigeria.

His older brother Seb, formerly in Chelsea’s academy as a goalkeeper, now plays NCAA Division I basketball for Loyola Maryland Greyhounds.
